note: Cnut the Great (ruled 1016–1035) assembled the North Sea Empire — England, Denmark, Norway, and nominally parts of Sweden — the largest empire in Northern Europe since the Romans. Cnut's empire linked the Viking and Anglo-Saxon worlds: he governed England with Anglo-Saxon institutions while maintaining Scandinavian kingship networks. The empire dissolved on his death (1035) through inheritance disputes among his sons. Harold Harefoot (England) and Sweyn (Norway) died young; Harthacnut's death (1042) ended the Danish line and restored the Wessex dynasty under Edward the Confessor.

_quarry.structural_significance: The only successful Norse empire in Britain; Cnut's use of English administrative institutions demonstrates Scandinavian rulers' capacity for governance adaptation; the empire's rapid dissolution shows the limits of personal dynastic empires without institutional continuity
